    nur ein Tempo (denn die b-Linie kann dem Weissen doch nicht mehr 
    streitig gemacht werden), sondern schwaecht auch die Diagonale b3-g8 
    unheilvoll.} )
17.Bg3 e5 {Baburin: 'This move is practically forced, as otherwise after 
Rfb1 White's would invade to b8. However, the text makes Black's position 
in the centre rather unstable.'} 
    ( 17...c5 18.Qb3 c4 19.Qb7 Bf5 20.f3 e5 21.e4 Be6 22.dxe5 fxe5 {kam 
    auch hier noch in Betracht,obwohl der Vorteil des Weissen ausser 
    Zweifel steht.} )
18.Rb7 Rf7 
    ( {Die Fortsetzung} 18...Bc8 19.Rxg7+ Kxg7 20.Qxc6 {Baburin: 'followed
    by 21 dxe5.'} 20...Rb8 21.dxe5 {laesst den Schwarzen zwischen den 
    Truemmern einer positionellen Ruine sitzen.} )
19.Rfb1 c5 {Mit grosser Verspaetung entschliesst sich Schwarz doch noch 
zur Durchfuehrung dieses Vorstosses, nachdem alle anderen Moeglichkeiten 
erschoepft sind.} 20.Qd1 Bc6 $2 
    ( 20...cxd4 21.cxd4 Be8 {war eher geeignet, die Aufgabe des Weissen zu
    erschweren, denn} 22.R7b6 Bb5 {ist jetzt nicht ratsam fuer den 
    Anziehenden.} )
21.R7b6 {Baburin: 'Without making obvious mistakes Black has got into 
serious trouble, as the pressure of White's rooks is very unpleasant. 
Meanwhile, Black's rooks are idle.'} 21...Qc7 {Schwarz kann sein wackliges
Zentrumsgebaeude nicht instand halten. Nach} 
    ( 21...Bb5 22.dxc5 Bxe2 23.Qxe2 Qc8 24.c6 Rc7 25.Qd1 Qe6 26.e4 dxe4 
        ( 26...Rd8 27.Rb8 Rcc8 28.c7 {ist nicht besser fuer Schwarz.} )
    27.Rb8+ Rc8 28.c7 {gewinnt der c-Bauer des Weissen entscheidende 
    Kraft.} )
22.dxe5 
    ( {It was also possible to take a pawn -} 22.Bxa6 {Baburin but White 
    decided to strike in the centre instead.} )
22...fxe5 23.e4 {'!' Baburin.} 23...d4 
    ( 23...Rd8 {war zaeher, doch ist die Stellung des Schwarzen nach} 24.
    exd5 Bxd5 25.Qa4 {nicht zu retten.} )
24.Bc4 Bxe4 25.Bxf7+ Kxf7 26.cxd4 Bxb1 
    ( 26...cxd4 27.Qb3+ Kf8 28.Re1 $18 )
27.Qf3+ 1-0

    ( 5.Qd2 b5 6.Bd3 Nd7 {guarding the e5 square is more common and more 
    wise.} )
5...Nf6 6.Qd2 b5 7.Bd3 $5 {This variation became extremly popular lately 
and as shows the following game black still didn't come up with proper 
answer.} 7...Bg4 8.e5 $1 {This move beyond any doubt is the most 
problematic for black.White has tried different continuation,but none of 
them promises clear advantage.Let's see a couple of examles:} 
    ( 8.Ng1 $5 e5 9.h3 exd4 10.Bxd4 Be6 11.a3 O-O 12.Nf3 a6 13.O-O c5 14.
    Be3 Re8 $11 {and black doesn't have any 
    problems;Hebden,M-Azmaiparashvili,Z;Oviedo 1993} )
    ( 8.O-O-O Nbd7 9.h3 Bxf3 10.gxf3 a5 11.f4 b4 12.Na4 Nb6 13.Nxb6 Qxb6 
    $132 {with very good counterplay;Adams,M-Hodgson,J;Hastings 1994} )
8...b4 9.Ne4 {The knight is much more usefull on e4,and in the following 
game we'llunderstand exactly why!} 
    ( 9.Ne2 $6 Nd5 10.Bh6 O-O 11.h4 Bxf3 12.gxf3 dxe5 13.h5 Bf6 $1 {The 
    only,but quiet sufficient defense.} 14.hxg6 hxg6 15.Bxf8 Qxf8 $44 {and
    black has strong counterplay due to darksquared 
    bishop;Apicella,M-Hickl,J; FRA-GER 1996} )
9...Nd5 {'?!' Ftacnik. Ftacnik: 'Black is to generous with time in a 
position where white enjoys good attacking chances. The exchange of 
knights must be the correct answer.'} 
    ( {Natural} 9...Nxe4 10.Bxe4 d5 
        ( 10...Bxf3 11.Bxf3 dxe5 12.O-O-O a5 13.d5 $1 {when black is in 
        trouble, e.g.} 13...Qc7 14.d6 exd6 15.Qxd6 Qxd6 16.Rxd6 {as white 
        will win back at least a pawn with advantage.} )
    11.Bd3 Bxf3 12.gxf3 a5 13.h4 Nd7 14.h5 Qb6 15.c4 $1 $16 {braught to 
    significient advantage of white in Leko,P-Beliavsky,A; Madrid 1998 so 
    black tries something else,but it proves to be even more dangerous.} )
10.Bh6 O-O 
    ( 10...Bxh6 11.Qxh6 Bxf3 12.gxf3 dxe5 
        ( 12...Qc7 13.Qg7 Rf8 14.exd6 exd6 15.Qxh7 Nd7 16.Qh4 $16 )
    13.dxe5 
        ( 13.Qg7 {Ftacnik} 13...Rf8 14.Ng5 Nf6 15.dxe5 Nh5 
            ( 15...Qd5 16.exf6 Qxg5 17.fxe7 Qxe7+ 18.Kf1 $18 )
        16.Qxh7 Qd5 17.O-O-O Qxe5 18.Nxf7 $1 Qf4+ 19.Kb1 Nf6 20.Bxg6 $18 )
    13...Qc7 14.Qg7 
        ( 14.e6 Qe5 $1 15.exf7+ Kxf7 16.O-O-O Qf4+ 17.Qxf4+ Nxf4 18.Bc4+ 
        $14 )
    14...Rf8 15.O-O-O Nf4 16.Bc4 $16 )
11.h4 $1 {McShane: 'The attack is very hard to deal with.'} 11...Bxf3 $2 {
After this move black's position is hopeless.Deserved attention} 
    ( 11...f5 $5 12.Bxg7 Kxg7 
        ( 12...fxe4 13.Bxf8 exd3 14.Bh6 Bxf3 15.gxf3 dxc2 16.Qxc2 $16 )
    13.Neg5 
        ( 13.Ng3 Bxf3 14.gxf3 f4 15.Ne4 dxe5 16.dxe5 Nd7 17.Ng5 Nxe5 18.
        O-O-O Qd7 $13 )
    13...Qc8 14.c4 bxc3 15.bxc3 $36 {with defendable position.} )
12.gxf3 $16 dxe5 
    ( {Doesn't work} 12...f5 13.Bxg7 Kxg7 14.Ng5 Qc8 15.h5 h6 16.hxg6 $1 
    hxg5 17.Qxg5 Rh8 18.O-O-O $18 {and white has decisive attack.} )
    ( 12...Re8 {Ftacnik} 13.h5 Bh8 14.hxg6 hxg6 15.e6 $1 $18 )
13.h5 {'!' McShane. McShane: 'White goes all out for the attack on the 
king.'} 13...Bf6 {It's hard to offer something better. Ftacnik: 'Black 
struggles to stay afloat in face of the model attack with opening of the h
file.'} 
    ( {Apart from} 13...Nf4 14.Bxg7 Kxg7 15.dxe5 Nxd3+ 
        ( 15...Nxh5 16.Rxh5 gxh5 17.Qg5+ Kh8 18.Nf6 exf6 19.Qf5 {wins} )
    16.cxd3 Rh8 17.Qxb4 {when white stands very well, there is no other 
    option, as the threat of hxg6 and Bxg7 followed by Qh6+ is very hard 
    to meet.} )
14.Nxf6+ exf6 15.hxg6 fxg6 16.Bxf8 Qxf8 {McShane: 'The smoke clears, 
leaving White an exchange up. Black hopes however that he has succeeded in
defusing the attack, but it's still alive and kicking. '} 17.dxe5 $18 {
White is an exchange up and in addition to it the attack is not over yet!}
17...Nd7 
    ( 17...fxe5 18.O-O-O Nd7 19.Bb5 $1 $18 )
18.Be4 N7b6 19.exf6 Qxf6 20.Qh6 {Ftacnik: 'What is black's compensation 
for the lost material?'} 20...Qf7 21.O-O-O Nf6 22.Bxg6 $1 1-0

1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.e3 c5 5.Ne2 cxd4 6.exd4 O-O 7.a3 Be7 8.d5 
exd5 9.cxd5 Bc5 10.Nd4 $6 {The more I look at this variation, the more I 
am convinced that if black is allowed to construct his 'standard' position
without interference he can look forward to a comfortable middle-game.} 
10...d6 11.Be2 a6 12.O-O Nbd7 13.Be3 {This seems a logical attempt to keep
this piece in the centre to contest the key dark squares, but as we shall 
see this is not the whole story! The older move was} 
    ( 13.Bg5 Re8 14.b4 
        ( 14.Nb3 Ba7 15.Nd2 h6 16.Bh4 Ne5 17.Nde4 g5 18.Nxf6+ Qxf6 19.Bg3 
        Bf5 20.Kh1 Ng6 21.Bg4 Nf4 $1 $15 {Sadler,M-Short,N/ch-GBR, Torquay
        ENG 1998.} )
    14...Ba7 15.Rc1 h6 16.Bh4 Nf8 17.h3 Bd7 18.Bg3 {It may be that g3, 
    pressuring black's only really discernable weakness, is after all the 
    best square for this piece.} 18...Rc8 19.Bf3 Qb6 20.Nb3 Ng6 21.Na5 Ne5
    22.Be2 Qd4 23.Qb3 Nd3 24.Bxd3 Qxd3 25.Bxd6 Bd4 26.Na2 Qxb3 27.Nxb3 Bb2
    28.Rxc8 Rxc8 29.Nc5 Bxa3 $11 {Lautier,J-Anand,V/Monte Carlo 1997/EXP 
    57.} )
13...Ne5 14.h3 Re8 15.b4 $6 {An understandable decision, since if white 
does not expand on the queen-side it is hard to suggest a plan. Still, the
weakness of c4 is by no means just theoretical.} 15...Bb6 {The choice of 
between b6 and a7 is here rather simply determined. Since there are 
potential tactics on the e3-a7 diagonal the bishop is most solidly placed 
on the square where its defender can stay put for some time. Since the a8 
rook is urgently needed to exploit white's 'looseness' on the c-file the 
queen best performs this role, and hence Topalov's move is the most 
logical.} 16.Qb3 {Choosing a square for the white queen is more tricky. 
The text is suitable for offering support to the weakened c4 square, and 
for promoting white's plan of pushing his queenside pawns ( it is 
difficult indeed to see another plan! ). On the other hand the d2 square 
might, as we shall see, be a more prudent choice for the less ambitious 
role of keeping white's centralised pieces well defended.} 16...Bd7 17.a4 
Rc8 18.Rac1 Ng6 $1 {I already prefer black, and it may be that even after 
a more prudent move such as} 19.Rfd1 $2 
    ( 19.Rfe1 {black can consider the positional sacrifice} 19...Rxe3 $5 
    20.fxe3 Qe7 21.Bf1 Qe5 $5 {with great play on the dark squares. 
    However, the text is clearly a mistake after which black gets decisive
    tactical threats instead of mere positional compensation.} )
19...Rxe3 $1 $17 {A beautiful resolution of the tension by which black 
shows that hissuperiority on the dark squares is not so latent after all.

    ( 7.Qd2 e5 8.d5 Nc5 )
    ( 7.Bd3 e5 8.d5 {is frequently played nowadays.} )
7...Qe8 
    ( {There is nothing wrong with the natural} 7...e5 {and after} 8.d5 
    Qe8 9.Ng3 {we reach the game continuation with transposition.} )

    ( 13.f3 Bf6 {/\ Qe7 Bg5} )
13...Nc5 14.Nd2 Bd7 15.Qc2 {This allows Black to simplify the position 
with exchanges.} 
    ( 15.Bxc5 {deserves attention to grab the |^ on the << at the expence 
    of giving away the nice dark-squared B, for example:} 15...dxc5 16.b4 
    Qe7 17.bxc5 Qxc5 18.Nb3 Qe7 19.c5 )
    ( {Without preparation} 15.b4 {is only a blow in the air:} 15...Na4 
    16.Nb5 $2 Bxb5 17.cxb5 Nc3 )

            ( 18...Nf6 19.Bg5 )
        19.g4 hxg3 20.fxg3 {/\ g4} )
    )
16...a6 17.Nxa4 Bxa4 18.b3 Bd7 19.Nc3 Qe7 20.Qc1 
    ( 20.O-O-O Bf6 {/\ Bg5} )
20...Rae8 
    ( 20...Bf6 $5 {comes into consideration.} 21.O-O 
        ( 21.exf5 Bxf5 
            ( 21...gxf5 22.O-O Bg5 23.f4 )
        22.O-O Bg5 $11 )
    21...Bg5 $11 
        ( 21...f4 {looks also dangerous, but after} 22.Bd2 Ng5 23.Qd1 {
        White can hold the blockade on the light squares.} )
    )
21.Ra2 
    ( {Here} 21.O-O {is more dangerous, than before:} 21...f4 22.Bd2 Ng5
